Here's the complete solution for turning your Flox environment into a Docker image.

## How it works

`flox containerize` packages your environment into an OCI image. The image's entrypoint **activates the environment on startup** — so all your installed packages, vars, and hooks are present, exactly like running `flox activate`. `docker run -it <image>` drops you into an activated shell; `docker run <image> <cmd>` runs a command inside the activated environment.

You only need the `[containerize.config]` block in your manifest if you want to set a default command, ports, user, etc. The plain commands work without it.

## Manifest

Add a `[containerize.config]` section to `.flox/env/manifest.toml` (everything in it is optional — include only what you need):

```toml
[install]
# ... your existing packages ...

[containerize.config]
cmd = ["bash"]                  # default command run inside the activated env; [] if a service should start instead
exposed-ports = ["8080/tcp"]    # ports to EXPOSE
user = "appuser"                # run as non-root (username or "uid:gid")
working-dir = "/app"            # initial working directory
volumes = ["/data"]             # mount points for persi

Here's the complete solution using Flox to produce a production Docker image — no Dockerfile needed. Flox builds an OCI image directly from your environment, so the image is reproducible and contains exactly the packages your environment pins.

## 1. Make sure your app runs in a Flox environment

If you don't already have one:

```bash
flox init
flox install python311   # or nodejs, etc. — whatever your app needs
```

Install your app's actual runtime dependencies into the environment (not dev-only tooling — keep the image lean).

## 2. Configure the container in the manifest

Run `flox edit` and add a `[containerize.config]` section. This is what makes the image production-ready (fixed start command, exposed port, non-root user, working dir). Example for a Python web app — adapt the `cmd`/port to your app:

```toml
[containerize.config]
# Command that runs when the container starts. It runs *inside* the
# activated Flox environment, so all packages/vars/hooks are available.
cmd = ["python", "-m", "myapp"]

# Port your server listens on (bind to 0.0.0.0 in your app, not localhost)
exposed-ports = ["8000/tcp"]

# Run as non-root in production
user = "app"

working-dir = "/app"

stop
